The index is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/curation/docs/index.json: url -> file, text, bytes, sha256, content_type, status, final_url, redirects, fetched_at. What was cached:
- 131 PDFs, each with `pdftotext -layout` text beside it (<file>.txt).
- 43 wiki HTML pages, each with its page-content text beside it (<file>.html.txt; table cells joined by " | ").
- The wiki sitemap, used only to find the exact page addresses.
- Responses by host: store.bblcdn.com 120, wiki.bambulab.com 44, cdn.shopify.com 9, store.bblcdn.eu 2.
- Every TDS and spec PDF was checked: its title matches its product.

Politeness:
- One sequential fetcher (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/curation/tools/fetch.py, run with `python3 -I`).
- Gaps per host are saved between runs: 6 s for wiki.bambulab.com, 1.5 s for every other host.
- User-Agent 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; LevonisCatalogImport/1.0; +https://levonis-iq.com)'; no cookies.
- Redirects are never followed automatically.
- robots.txt was read first for every host:
  - wiki.bambulab.com: 200, empty.
  - cdn.shopify.com: 200; nothing disallowed for these files.
  - store.bblcdn.com and store.bblcdn.eu: 403 S3 AccessDenied (the robots.txt object does not exist). RFC 9309 treats this as no restriction.
  - e.bambulab.com: 404.
- us.store.bambulab.com and levonis-iq.com were never contacted. All store pages were parsed offline from the corpus with packages/catalog/src/bambuImport (extractPage plus describe; the script is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/curation/tools/collect-links.ts, run from /home/user/levonis-curated).
- No 429s or challenge pages.
- Everything is resumable: URLs already in index.json are skipped.

STOP EVENT: public-cdn.bambulab.com answered 403 to GET /robots.txt at 2026-10-16T08:21:37Z. The body was not an S3 missing-object response, so the fetcher stopped. I did not retry or probe that host again. I marked it blocked (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/curation/robots/public-cdn.bambulab.com.status) and resumed the run on the other hosts, which were all answering 200. The cost is one document: refurbished-x1c's 'X1-Carbon tech specs.pdf'. If that 403 should have halted the whole job rather than just that host, nothing else was affected, but you should know it was a judgement call.

Which documents were cached, by product type:
- Filaments: TDS, SDS and hex PDFs linked by the store page; the material table; the matching /en/filament/<family> page; dry-filament; and the filament-specific guides the store page links (pva, asa-aero, support-for-abs, tpu-85a-90a, pla-pure).

- Build plates: the material table and the plates page, plus 3d-effect-sheets and cool-plate-supertack pages.

- Deliberately not cached:

  - Maintenance and generic how-to wiki pages.

problems: RUNNER BUG (blocks the write): mergeCurated never copies a curated spec's source_url. PayloadSpec has no source_ref, and mergeCurated sets checked_sources to []. The writer's specSourceRef takes source_ref from checked_sources for every kind other than store_page, store_messages and derived. So all 50 verified store_doc rows in this file get source_ref '' and break the 0194 CHECK (status <> 'verified' OR source_ref <> ''). assertImportPayload still passes, so the failure only shows up when product_spec_values is inserted at /write. This hits every curated file with verified tds, sds, manual, wiki or store_doc rows.

False conflicts in mergeCurated: when value_num is null it compares value_text and ignores value_bool. Six boolean rows (chamber_heating, door_sensor, filament_runout_sensor, filament_tangle_sensor, filament_odometry, power_loss_recovery) have curated true against the page's 'Supported' (value_bool 1 on both sides). Each one is marked 'curated value differs' and adds a spec_sources_disagree note even though the values agree. Simulated merge: specs_added 10, specs_replaced 51, conflicts 7.

printing.supported_filament has a real difference in how the value is written, and it carries a conflict_note. The store table puts the material list in the label cell and 'Supported' in the value cell, so the page parse stores one run-on item ending in '— Supported'. The curated list writes 'Carbon/Glass Fiber Reinforced PLA/PETG/PA/PET/PC/ABS/ASA' as one item. That grouping is my reading of the spec sheet's run-on list, so the second-agent check should look at it.

in_the_box (25 items, the H2D AMS Combo column of the official wiki packing list, scoped to option value 776282589202808833) and relations (9) are not applied by mergeCurated (not_applied 34). The page's own package.contents therefore stays. That list mixes every combo: H2D Laser Full Combo, Laser Edition, the 10W and 40W Laser Modules, Cutting Module, Laser Platform, and 'Emergency' and 'Stop Button' as two separate items. This product's only version is the H2D AMS Combo.

in_the_box comes from the packing list for a NEW H2D AMS Combo (wiki updated 2026-09-30). The refurbished page says units are 'Repackaged with all the original accessories — manual, cables, and box'. The owner or a reviewer should confirm the list applies to the refurbished unit.

The curated documents entry for the PDF (spec_sheet, 'H2D Spec Sheet') is dropped as a duplicate URL of the page's document row. documentKindOf files that row as kind 'tds' with title 'TDS' because of its link text. Customers would see the H2D Spec Sheet labelled as a technical data sheet (TDS).

The page's laser and cutting rows are stored at product scope: 31 x.* rows for the 10W & 40W Laser Module and the Cutting Module, plus Laser Safety Windows and Air Assist Pump. They describe Laser Edition equipment that the AMS Combo does not include. They have no registry keys, so the curated file cannot override them. printing.camera_birdseye is Laser Edition only; it is recorded with test_condition 'H2D Laser Edition only' and a note.

Six spec-sheet quotes come from multi-line PDF cells: build_volume, extruder_motor, max_flow, max_flow_high_flow, supported_filament and software. Each quote is the cell's words in reading order. pdftotext interleaves the row label with the cell's lines, so these quotes are not exact substrings of the cached .txt. The 220 V values are cell texts from messages.production.H2D, resolved through the package's RSC parser.

Following §C.6, the 220 V values come from the page's messages bundle (source_kind store_messages, official_page, intl_220v): electrical.voltage, electrical.frequency, electrical.max_power, package.length, package.width and package.height (620×620×755 mm, from 'Physical Dimensions Asia'), and shipment.gross_weight 42.3 kg scoped to H2D AMS Combo (from 'Gross Weight UK'). electrical.rated_power (Average Power 1050 W) appears only in the spec sheet, so its intl_220v row is store_doc and verified. Each us_110v row is unverified and has test_condition 'US version (100–120 V)'.

Relation evidence for AMS 2 Pro, AMS HT, first-generation AMS, AMS lite (not compatible) and the 4-in-1 PTFE Adapter comes from the store page FAQ and feature note, so it cites the store canonical URL, which is owner-only provenance. The 'requires 4-in-1 PTFE Adapter' relation only applies when more than 2 AMS units are connected. That condition is kept only in an extra 'condition' field, and product_relations has no column for it.

The file adds fields that the §F example does not have: conflict_note and note on specs, condition on one relation, scope, section and locator on in_the_box items, and retrieved_at and locator on searched entries. mergeCurated ignores them. A strict schema test may need to allow them.

No other documents were cached or used. No user manual or quick-start PDF was available, and the page's bambulab.com/h2d 'Learn More' link was not fetched (offline). Nothing needed for this file was missing.

RUNNER BLOCKER (not in the file): mergeCurated drops each spec's source_url. PayloadSpec has no source_ref, and the writer's specSourceRef reads checked_sources[0].url, which is [] for curated rows. I ran the merge on the parsed h2d payload: 52 verified store_doc rows would be written with source_ref ''. That breaks 0194's CHECK (status <> 'verified' OR source_ref <> '') and the batch fails. Fix in enrich.ts: carry raw.source_url, for example as checked_sources [{kind, url, title}].

RUNNER (false conflicts): mergeCurated compares value_text whenever value_num is null. A curated boolean true becomes 'Yes', the store page row says 'Supported', so it flags a disagreement. Result: 6 false spec_sources_disagree notes and conflict flags on thermal.chamber_heating, printing.door_sensor, filament_runout_sensor, filament_tangle_sensor, filament_odometry and power_loss_recovery. The values do agree. Fix: compare value_bool when both rows are booleans. The 7th conflict, printing.supported_filament, is real and carries a conflict note.

RUNNER (object values): valueFields has no {x,y,z} form. An object value is skipped, and an array gives the text '325, 320, 325' plus a false conflict. So printing.build_volume is written as the text '325 × 320 × 325 mm', which matches the store page row exactly; its value_list stays empty.

Checks run with the runner's mergeCurated on the payload the package built from the cached page: assertImportPayload passes; skipped 0 (every scope resolved); 51 replaced, 13 added, 17 not_published rows; documents +1 (the wiki page; TDS.pdf deduplicated); relations, in_the_box and hex are not applied (not_applied 20).

Every key is in the registry with the registry's unit. Weights are written in g; the merge renders them as published ('31 kg', '38.5 kg'). Every value has a locator and a quote of at most 200 characters. Every PDF quote was checked verbatim against the PDF tables; the messages, store-page and wiki quotes were checked against their sources. Ranges are sane (nozzle 350 °C, bed 120 °C, chamber 65 °C). Every not_published key is covered by a searched entry. No price, cost, stock or shipping value; buying-advice tails were cut from quotes.

DOCUMENT KIND: TDS.pdf is labelled 'TDS' by the store link and its file name, so documentKindOf returns 'tds' and customers will see it titled as a technical data sheet. It is actually the 3-page 'H2D Spec Sheet'. Its values use source_kind 'store_doc' with confidence official_doc; test_method/test_condition are filled only where the sheet gives conditions (max flow test parameters, max power footnote, single-nozzle build volume, 'with AMS', Laser Edition).

REGION: the sheet states both voltages. The 220 V values (voltage, frequency, max power 2200 W, average power 1050 W) are intl_220v and verified. The 110 V values are us_110v and unverified, with 'US version (100–120 V)'. The intl_220v package (620×620×755 mm) and gross weights (H2D 38.5, AMS Combo 42.3, Laser Full Combo 46.2 kg) come from messages.production.H2D 'Physical Dimensions Asia' and 'Gross Weight Asia' (store_messages, official_page). Source quirk: the messages 'Specs Table No Collapse 110V' table itself carries the UK gross weights; the rendered US page shows 40.6/44.2/48.2 kg.
CBM: the intl_220v box enters only through the curated merge, which runs after the builder's deriveCbm. So no package.volume_m3 is derived from it at run time.

SCOPE: the gross weights are scoped, as the source words them, to the version value 'H2D AMS Combo'. That value also covers the Dual AMS 2 Pro and AMS HT bundle variants, whose extra AMS box the published figure does not include. The store-page parse scopes them the same way.

REGISTRY GAPS, so no curated row: dual-nozzle volume 300×320×325 and two-nozzle total 350×320×325 (the store's headline 'Print Volume'; the store notes say it needs identical filament in both nozzles); the Laser Safety Windows and Air Assist Pump rows; about 30 rows for the 10W/40W laser module and the cutting module (p.2–3). These stay as the store page's unverified x.* rows.

printing.supported_filament: the row is malformed in both the PDF and the store table (the list sits in the label column, with a third cell 'Supported'). It is written unverified, split at the document's commas, with the reinforced group kept as one item and a conflict note. The store row was one unsplit item.

Added from the parsed store page because the deterministic layer misses them: safety.certifications ('Cybersecurity compliant with EU RED Article 3.3(d)(e) and ETSI EN 303 645 V2.1.1:2020', store_page, unverified). Relations from the FAQ, feature footnotes and notes: AMS (first generation) compatible but without drying; AMS lite not compatible; AMS 2 Pro (up to 4) and AMS HT (up to 8); 4-in-1 PTFE Adapter required above 2 AMS. From the PDF: Laser Upgrade Kit for the H2D and AMS Combo versions, and the Textured and Smooth PEI plates. From the wiki: an external power adapter for AMS 2 Pro units used for drying, target handle ams-2-pro-switching-adapter taken from the wiki link rather than named in the text.

IN THE BOX comes only from the official wiki table: Laser Full Combo, the AMS Combo Standard variant, H2D, plus the two bundle add-ons. The wiki's Laser Full Combo column does not list the 10W/40W laser module itself; only the store page's own box list names it.

NOT_PUBLISHED left out on purpose, so neither a value nor not_published: auto_leveling (the store notes mention a 3D mesh feature), filament_cutter (the wiki lists an H2D filament cutter), multi_color (the FAQ states multi-colour printing with AMS), included_build_plate (named in the store box list), safety.certifications (has a value). Also left out are model-specific or irrelevant keys: main/aux hotend lists and extruders, battery, connector, requirements, carton.*, volume_m3, working_area, outer_frame, interface, wireless_network.

NOT SEARCHED: bambulab.com/h2d (the page's 'Learn More' link; not cached, bot challenge, never fetched). The not_published claims (noise, Bluetooth, Ethernet, layer height and others) therefore rest only on the spec sheet, the store page and its messages bundle, which is what checked_sources lists. Nothing else I needed was missing from the cache.

Some facts have no registry key that applies to type ams, so they are not written as specs and are not listed as not_published. From the spec sheet and wiki: Drying › Highest Temperature 65 °C (reached only at ambient ≥ 25 °C), the drying-supported filament list (a * means it needs a higher temperature than 65 °C), Active Moisture Discharge, Sealed Storage, Temperature and Humidity Detection, RFID Identification (2 RFID coils), Spool Dimension (width 50–68 mm, diameter 197–202 mm) and the two drying modules. The drying.* keys apply to filament only. I did not use thermal.chamber_temp for the drying temperature because its meaning is different. The registry should get keys for these before the run.

Store page parser gap: the messages.SpecificationTable fields spoolDimension*, rfidIdentification, filamentSupportedDryingValue, activeMoistureDischarge, sealedStorage, temperatureHumidity* and powerInputValue ('24 V 4 A') produce no row, not even an x.* row. 'Highest Temperature' becomes x.highest_temperature '* 65 °C' with status unverified. Curated electrical.voltage '24 V' and electrical.current '4 A' come from the spec sheet; the page has no row for them, so there is nothing to conflict with.

Store page parser gap: the builder's package.contents keeps only 1 of the 4 items in the page's What's in the Box list ('Bambu AMS 2 Pro'). The curated in_the_box lists all 4: AMS 2 Pro, Desiccant, PTFE Tube (185mm*2+225mm*2+900mm*1) and Bambu Bus Cable-6Pin. mergeCurated does not apply in_the_box, relations or hex, so the payload still has 1 item. I added no package.contents spec, because one would only conflict at the same rank.

The builder files the spec PDF as kind 'tds' with the title 'TDS' (from the link text 'Download TDS'). It is the 'AMS 2 Pro Spec Sheet'. The curated documents entry (kind spec_sheet) cannot change this, because documentRow builds the same id from the URL and the existing row is kept.

Two conflicts are intentional and each carries a conflict_note: printing.supported_filament and printing.unsupported_filament. The curated lists split the sheet's run-on lists ('Bambu PLA-CF/PAHT-CF/PETG-CF/Support for PLA/PETG' becomes 4 items, 'Bambu PET-CF/TPU 95A' becomes 2) and drop the 'and'. The materials are the same. The merge records them as spec_sources_disagree, and the curated value wins on rank. Every other value that is also on the store page agrees: dimensions 372×280×226 mm, 2.5 kg, ABS/PC, 1.75 mm.

Unclear which 4-in-1 PTFE Adapter version is meant. For H2D/H2C the store says '4-in-1 PTFE Adapter II (SA014)' and the wiki says the H2C needs the H2 series dedicated version. For X2D the wiki contradicts itself ('adapter II' in its X2D section, 'standard' in its Types note) and the store variant note says FAZ013-N. Both the deterministic relations and the curated ones point at the handle bambu-4-in-1-ptfe-adapter without naming its option value. A reviewer has to decide.

The store's option value 'A2 Series' is treated as the A2L: the wiki documents only the A2L, and the store's own variant notes for that value name the A2L. The A2 Series ams.max_units row and its relations rest on the A2L section.

electrical.voltage and electrical.current are written with region '' because the 24 V 4 A rating is the unit's power input and the spec sheet has no US 100–120 V wording. electrical.* is flagged regionDependent 'always', so the reviewer should confirm this.
No AMS 2 Pro acc-in-the-box wiki page was in the cached set, so in_the_box comes from the store page's official list only. Nothing was fetched (offline).

Self-check passed. Every quote was matched against the cached text of its document (≤ 200 chars). Every key is in the registry, applies to ams and has the registry's unit and type. Every verified numeric value has a locator and a quote. All 10 not_published keys are covered by a searched entry. Ranges are sane. A simulated mergeCurated on the payload built from the corpus page gave: specs_added 11, specs_replaced 8, conflicts 2, not_published 10, documents 4, skipped 0, not_applied 32 (28 relations + 4 box items).

Self-check passed. I checked the registry keys, units, applies-to-filament and ranges. I checked locator and quote (200 characters or fewer) on all 20 verified TDS values, and that both not_published keys (material.length, mechanical.hardness) are covered by searched entries (TDS, SDS, store page and wiki). On the parsed store page the two values that overlap agree: material.diameter is 1.75 mm, and material.net_weight is 1000 g on option value 1kg (564681938135969824). The runner's own mergeCurated ran on the payload built from the corpus page (extractPage + buildImportPayload with the manifest row and identity-map entry): 16 specs added, 3 replaced (diameter, density, nozzle_temp, which were not_found), 0 conflicts, 0 skipped, 2 not_published, 2 wiki documents added. assertImportPayload passed on the merged payload.

The certificate PDFs (RoHS, POPs, CP65, TSCA, SVHC, PAHs, EN71-3) are not cached; the fetch plan skipped them. So safety.certifications is not curated, and it is not listed as not_published. The store page's 'certified to UL GREENGUARD 2904' is page prose only.

The registry has one key per scope and region, so the mechanical.* keys hold the TDS X-Y printed-specimen values. The Z values are not stored: tensile 31 MPa, elongation 7.5 %, bending modulus 2370 MPa, bending strength 59 MPa, impact 13.8 kJ/m².

The registry has no *.printed / *.material key pairs. The split is carried by the key group: mechanical.* holds printed specimens, and material.density and thermal.* hold material properties. test_condition says which. The TDS does not say whether its HDT and Vicat specimens were printed.

There are two HDT rows. I stored ISO 75 at 1.8 MPa (54 °C); the 0.45 MPa value (57 °C) appears only in test_condition. The impact value is the cell's first figure (26.6 kJ/m²); the notched 7.9 kJ/m² appears in test_condition.

print_settings.print_speed is a range key, but it holds the text '< 300 mm/s' (value_num null) because the TDS gives only an upper bound. The store page's 'up to 258mm/s*' is marketing and was not used.

These TDS facts have no registry key and are not stored: Young's modulus, melt index, saturated water absorption, spool material and size (ABS, 200 x 67 mm), retraction length and speed, chamber temperature, max overhang and bridging, printing and storage humidity, support material, and crystallization temperature (N/A).

Generic-PLA wiki values differ from the product TDS: nozzle 190-240 °C against 190-230 °C, and oven drying 55 °C against 50 °C. I kept the TDS values; the drying wiki's PLA Basic row agrees with the TDS. Each difference is recorded in a per-spec 'conflict' field. mergeCurated does not read that field, nor 'note', top-level 'notes', hex source_value_id, or relation locator and target_family.

mergeCurated does not apply the hex (30 colours, all 30 store colour values matched by position in the PDF), relations (7) or in_the_box (empty: there is no official packing list) sections. It counts them as not_applied, 37 in total.

The relations to 'Cool Plate' and to '0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 mm nozzles' name no target handle; there is no matching store product. 'High Temperature Plate' was mapped to bambu-smooth-pei-plate based on the wiki column header 'Bambu Smooth PEI / High-Temperature Plate'.
The hex-code document's searched entry has keys [] because it was read for hex codes only. The SDS model 'A00-xx' was not stored as identity.model, because the identity map gives 'PLA Basic'.

CONFLICT, needs the owner: the two sources give different values for thermal.max_nozzle_temp. The store page's Product Specifications says 'Max. Printing Temp. 320 ℃'. The nozzles wiki's A Series Nozzle panel says 'Max. Printing Temp: 300 ℃' and names A2L/A1/A1 mini. The wiki value is recorded as verified at confidence official_page, the same rank the runner gives wiki tables. So mergeCurated keeps the store's 320 °C, sets the row's conflict and writes one spec_sources_disagree note. problems: The registry has no laser-machine keys. These official R1 values are left out of specs and have no key to go under: Max cutting capacity per lens (short focus 15 mm black walnut / 20 mm acrylic; medium and long focus 18 mm / 20 mm), Spot size per lens (Ø0.11 / 0.17 / 0.19 mm), Absolute motion accuracy (<0.1 mm @600 mm), Air assist pump (30 L/min @30 kPa), Positioning system and accuracy (<0.2 mm), panoramic and detail capture, focusing, toolhead positioning, curved, cylinder and revolve processing, the Automation rows, safety interlocks, safety key, emergency stop, and Max material size (store table only: 710 × 380 mm standalone, up to 610 mm wide with the Conveyor). The FAQ also gives laser wavelength 9–11 µm and processing height 0–58 mm (up to 248 mm with the riser base); these are also left out.
Laser type '55W CO2 laser' is stored under printing.technology because no laser key exists. Its label will read 'Printing technology'.
Supported materials have no spec key. They are written as relations instead: 10 compatible_with material relations plus not_compatible_with 'Bare (uncoated) metal', all from the spec sheet p.1.

'Weight 33.5kg' (spec sheet p.2) is written as product.net_weight 33500 g with status unverified. The sheet does not say whether it is net or gross. Also, the registry's product.net_weight appliesTo leaves out laser_machine, so a schema test that checks appliesTo will reject this row. An adjudicator should decide whether to keep or drop it.

Several printer-only keys have empty appliesTo, so they formally apply to laser_machine: build_volume, layer_height, build_plate, supported/unsupported_filament, filament sensors, multi_color, auto_leveling, max_flow, extruder_*, supported_nozzle_diameters, max_nozzle/bed/chamber temps, steady_state_power. They are deliberately left out of not_published, because it would be wrong to say a laser cutter's manufacturer did not publish them. printing.camera, connectivity.storage, package.weight and shipment.gross_weight are also left out of both lists: the documents hint at them but are ambiguous ('Dual-camera' positioning system, 'USB Supported', the unlabelled 'Weight').

Package extractor gap: DESCRIPTION_KEYS does not include richText, descriptionTypeStyles or downloadButton/downloadUrl. Because of this, the parsed store payload for r1 has 0 specs, 0 documents and no in-the-box. The R1 Specs table with its footnotes 1–4 (flight row 162), the per-version What's in the box table (flight row 161) and the R1_Spec.pdf Download PDF link never reach the builder. I read them from the raw flight. The table agrees with the PDF row by row and adds one extra row (max material size). The curated documents[] adds the PDF link.
Consistency: the parsed store page has no spec rows to conflict with. The highlights prose (600 × 300 mm, 1000 mm/s, 20,000 mm/s², 0.2 mm) agrees with the curated values.
Region: R1 has one universal input, '100–240 VAC, 50/60Hz', and its messages bundle has no R1 namespace and no 110 V or 220 V values. So electrical rows use region '' (no intl_220v or us_110v rows).
Package dimensions (1095×725×310 mm) are scoped to the 'R1' version only. The bundles add the Riser Base, Conveyor and Rotary items, and their packaging is not published.

In-the-box differences between sources: the store table lists 'Allen Key ×1', while the wiki names 'H2.0 & H1.5 Allen Keys'. The store table lists 'Lubricant Grease ×2' and 'Lubricant Oil ×1', while the wiki has one combined 'Lubricant Oil & Grease' entry.

Not cached and not read: the wiki pages linked from the store FAQ (https://wiki.bambulab.com/en/r1/manual/focusing-lens-guide and https://wiki.bambulab.com/en/r1/manual/laser-alignment-guide). They are not in documents[]. No R1 manual or TDS was among the cached documents.

The reviewed compat-targets labels have no Riser Base, Conveyor, E1 Pro or Fire Extinguishing entries, so the 8 accessory relations carry manifest handles in target_source_handle but will not resolve through compat-targets. identity-map.json has no r1 entry.

The registry has no *.printed / *.material key pairs, so mechanical.* holds printed-specimen X-Y results, and density, melting point and glass transition (the 'material property' rows) are raw-material values. The TDS does not say what form the HDT and Vicat specimens take, and test_condition says so.

Both values that also appear on the store page agree: diameter 1.75 mm and net weight 1 kg. The net-weight row is scoped to the option value '1kg' (source_value_id 564681886055297030), so the page's official_variant row wins by rank, with the same value and no conflict.

A trial run of the runner's mergeCurated on the package-parsed page added 18 specs, replaced 3, wrote 2 not_published rows and added 2 documents. It found 0 conflicts and skipped 0 specs. It does not apply relations, hex or in_the_box (6 relations not applied).

not_published is limited to filament-specific registry keys: material.length and mechanical.hardness. Generic any-type keys (package.*, shipment.*, identity.series/family) are not listed. The diameter tolerance (± 0.03 mm) comes only from the store page and is left to the deterministic layer.

The not_compatible_with hotend relations use the store page's canonical URL as source_url (owner-only provenance), with the PLA wiki as corroborating evidence. The SDS gives no numeric properties ('No data available' for density and melting point); only identity.model 'A11-xx' is taken from it.

Self-check passed: the file ran through the runner's own mergeCurated (/home/user/levonis-runner/scripts/bambu-import/enrich.ts) against the page parsed by the package from corpus/p0/raw/tpu-95a-hf.html.gz with the manifest row. Result: 13 specs added, 3 replaced, 0 conflicts, 6 not_published, 1 document added, 0 skipped, 23 parts not applied (6 hex + 17 relations). Every key is in the registry with the registry's unit. Every verified value has a locator and a quote of 200 characters or fewer, and every quote appears word for word in the source text in pdftotext -raw reading order. Ranges are sane. All 6 not_published keys are covered by a searched entry.

Agreement with the store page: material.diameter 1.75 mm agrees. material.net_weight is scoped to option value '1 kg' (source_value_id 564681959094906895) and agrees with the page's 1000 g row, which outranks it (official_variant), so the page row stays. The page's not_found rows for material.density and print_settings.nozzle_temp are replaced by TDS values. AMS not_compatible agrees with the page bullet 'All AMS Series NOT Compatible'. material.diameter_tolerance (±0.03 mm) is on the store page only: it is not curated and not listed as not_published.

Conflicts between documents, noted in each entry's 'conflict' field: print_settings.nozzle_temp is 220-240 °C in the TDS but 200-250 °C (±10 °C) in the wiki material table; print_settings.bed_temp is 30-35 °C in the TDS but differs per plate in the wiki (Engineering 30-35, Smooth PEI/High Temperature 35-45, Textured PEI 35-45, 30-45 with glue); print_settings.recommended_plate and the 'Cool Plate' relation: the TDS lists Cool Plate, but the wiki marks TPU on Cool Plate / PLA Plate as 'Not recommended'. The TDS value is kept in every case. Drying (70 °C, 8 h in an oven) agrees with the wiki drying page Appendix I.

Two values with a published bound are stored as text so the bound is not lost: mechanical.elongation_at_break '> 650%' (registry type number) and print_settings.print_speed '< 200 mm/s' (registry type range). If the schema test requires a number or range type, this needs a decision.
mechanical.hardness '95A' is UNVERIFIED. It is read only from the product name 'TPU 95A HF'; no document has a Shore hardness row.

TDS facts with no registry key (not stored): Z-direction tensile strength 22.3 ± 0.6 MPa, elongation > 480% and impact strength 86.3 kJ/m²; Young's modulus X-Y 9.8 ± 0.7 MPa and Z 7.4 ± 0.6 MPa; melt index 36.5 ± 2.6 g/10 min (210 °C, 2.16 kg); crystallization temperature N/A; water absorption 1.08% (25 °C, 55% RH); spool material PC + ABS (temperature resistance 90 °C); spool size 200 mm diameter, 67 mm height; printing and storage humidity < 20% RH; retraction length 0.8-1.4 mm and speed 20-40 mm/s; chamber temperature 25-45 °C (thermal.chamber_temp is a printer number key, so it was not used); max overhang about 55°; max bridging 20 mm; second drying method on an X1 heatbed 80-90 °C for 12 h (kept in test_condition); odor, chemical resistance and flammability rows. All mechanical values used are X-Y printed specimens; their test_condition records the specimen print settings and the 70 °C, 12 h annealing.

Not cached, so not read: the 'Filament RoHS' certificate linked from the store page (https://store.bblcdn.com/925d913ab89b4707990b5c00cc239c52.pdf). safety.certifications is therefore neither curated nor listed as not_published. Also not available: a /en/filament/<family> wiki page for TPU 95A HF, and the 'TPU Printing Guide' that the store FAQ names without a link.
Identity mismatch for the owner: the SDS gives 'Model: U01-xx', but the manifest SKU codes are U00-K0/W0/D0/Y0/B0/R0-1.75-1000-SPL. Not stored as a spec.
Store page copy error: the FAQ safety tips say 'this filament contains highly hygroscopic wood fibers', which does not apply to TPU. It is customer-facing prose and was not used here.

Two relations (not_compatible_with 'Hotend with Stainless Steel Nozzle 0.2 mm' and 'Cool Plate SuperTack') cite the store page FAQ, so their source_url is the store canonical URL, which is owner-only provenance. The wiki only marks the 0.2 mm nozzle 'Not Recommended'. The bed-surface note 'Glue' is stored as recommended_with, not requires. in_the_box is empty because no official in-the-box list exists for this filament. The SDS states no numeric properties (density and melting point say 'No data available').

The store page lists a 'Filament RoHS' document (https://store.bblcdn.com/2c7b9c30a9014c65bb4aeacd9c70e6af.pdf) that is not in the cache and was not read. So safety.certifications is neither written nor listed as not_published.

Official sources conflict on print_settings.nozzle_temp. The TDS (p.1) gives 190 - 230 °C. The wiki filament guide nozzle table (PLA Glow row) gives 210 - 240 °C (±10 °C). The TDS value is kept (official_doc) and the conflict is recorded in the spec's note. The store page states no nozzle temperature.

Official sources conflict on AMS compatibility. The store page says 'AMS 2 Pro, AMS HT & AMS Compatible, but can lead to faster wear'. The wiki filament guide AMS table says PLA Glow is 'Not Recommended' for AMS / AMS lite, and warns that glow filaments grind down the AMS PTFE tubes. The compatible_with relations keep the store page wording and carry the wiki disagreement as a note.

print_settings.print_speed is a range key, but the TDS gives only an upper bound: 'Printing Speed < 250 mm/s'. mergeCurated cannot write a value with only an upper bound: a bare number would drop the '<', and a range would need an invented lower bound. It is therefore kept as text with status unverified (the §C.6 rule for unparseable values), and a schema test that checks value types strictly may flag it.

These TDS facts have no fitting registry key and were not written: Chamber Temperature 25 - 45 °C (thermal.chamber_temp is a number key, while this is a recommended range); every Z-direction mechanical value; Young's modulus 2030/1750 MPa; Melt Index 23.3 g/10 min; Saturated Water Absorption 0.46%; Printing and Storage Humidity < 20% RH; retraction length and speed; overhang and bridging; Bed Surface Preparation Glue; spool material PC + ABS (90 °C) and spool size 200 x 67 mm; annealing 50-60 °C for 6-12 h. They are listed in the file's notes.
thermal.heat_deflection_temp holds one value: the 0.45 MPa row, 55 °C. The second TDS row (ISO 75, 1.8 MPa: 52 °C) is recorded only in the spec's note.
The SDS model code 'A12-xx' is not written as identity.model, because the identity map already sets identity.model to 'PLA Glow' and a curated official_doc value would replace it.

Nine quotes rebuild a table row whose cell text the PDF layout splits across lines or into two columns: impact strength, recommended plate, drying temperature and drying time, and 4 of the 5 hex entries. The words are verbatim, but these quotes are not single contiguous strings in the pdftotext output.

mergeCurated currently records hex (5), relations (12) and in_the_box (0) as not_applied (17 items), so they reach the payload only when the writer supports them. in_the_box is empty because no searched document gives an official in-the-box list.

Dry run of the runner's mergeCurated on the store page payload, parsed with the package (manifest row, identity map, compat targets, media overrides): 18 specs added, 3 replaced (two store page not_found rows, density and nozzle_temp, plus diameter), 0 conflicts, 0 skipped, net_weight's option_value scope resolved, 2 not_published rows with checked sources. Store page values that agree: diameter 1.75 mm and net weight 1 kg.

Three documents linked from the store page are not cached, so I did not read them: the RoHS certificate (https://store.bblcdn.com/45e0bfd4faf34c3db8a0f3a1ed264727.pdf) and two wiki pages (/en/knowledge-sharing/transparent-petg and /en/general/swaping-new-filament-with-bambu-reusable-spool). Because of this, safety.certifications is left unset: it is neither a spec nor in not_published.

The sources disagree on the 0.2 mm nozzle. The TDS Nozzle Size row lists 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 mm. The store page FAQ says 'Not compatible with Hotend with Stainless Steel Nozzle 0.2 mm.', the wiki material table marks the 0.2 mm nozzle 'Not Compatible', and the PETG wiki page says '(excluding 0.2 mm)'. I stored extrusion.supported_nozzle_diameters as unverified with a conflict note, and added a not_compatible_with '0.2 mm Nozzle' relation with wiki-table evidence. This needs a decision before commit.

The wiki differs from the TDS on two settings. Nozzle temperature: the wiki says 230-260 °C (±10 °C), the TDS says 230-270 °C. Bed temperature: the wiki says 60-80 °C, the TDS says 65-75 °C. I kept the TDS values as verified and added notes. Drying at 65 °C for 8 h in a blast drying oven matches the wiki.
Clear (32101) has no hex code in the official Hex Code Table, which lists 8 colours. The store page offers 9 colour values, so the file has hex codes for 8 colours.

These TDS values have no registry key and were not stored: the Z-direction mechanical values (tensile 29, elongation 5.2 %, bending strength 55, bending modulus 1520, impact 7.2), the heat deflection temperature of 68 °C at 1.8 MPa, the notched X-Y impact value of 8.6 kJ/m², Young's modulus (1420 / 1230 MPa), melt index 11.7 g/10 min, saturated water absorption 0.30 %, printing and storage humidity < 20 % RH, retraction length 0.8-1.4 mm and speed 30-60 mm/s, max overhang ~70°, max bridging ~30 mm, glue as bed surface preparation, the spool's ABS material (70 °C) and size (200 x 67 mm), heatbed drying on the X1 Series at 75-85 °C for 12 h, and the chemical-resistance rows. I did not use material.spool_type for the spool details, because its template field only accepts Refill, With spool or Cardboard.

Choices I made where the registry has one row per key: heat deflection temperature uses the 0.45 MPa value (74 °C), not the 1.8 MPa value. Impact strength uses the X-Y value the TDS does not mark as notched (37.4 kJ/m²). Mechanical keys take the X-Y values, with test_condition saying they come from printed specimens and giving the specimen settings. Net weight is scoped to option value 564681962920112152 ('1 kg'), so it merges with the page row: equal values, and the page row stays. Print speed is stored as the text '< 220 mm/s', because the TDS gives no minimum. thermal.chamber_temp holds the recommended range of 35-50 °C. identity.model 'G01-xx' comes from the SDS.

not_published lists only filament-specific registry keys the documents do not state: material.length and mechanical.hardness. I did not list the general printer and logistics keys whose appliesTo is empty. material.diameter_tolerance (±0.03 mm) is published on the store page only, so it is not in not_published.

Store-page agreement: diameter 1.75 mm and net weight 1000 g agree. A simulated mergeCurated against the parsed page gave 19 rows added, 3 replaced (diameter, density, nozzle temperature), 0 conflicts, 0 skipped and 2 not_published rows, and the merged payload passes assertImportPayload. Some fields in the file are for the reviewers only and mergeCurated ignores them: 'note' and 'conflict' on specs, 'quote' on hex entries, and 'scope', 'locator' and 'target_kind' on relations.

Hex codes and relations are reported as not_applied by mergeCurated (12 entries), which is expected. The compat-targets.json in /home/user/levonis-curated is empty, so the parsed page's own 'AMS Series' relation came out unresolvable.
